**Hans-Joachim Merker** (7 October 1929 – 18 August 2014)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merker#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merker#cite_note-BaumgartenHG-2) was a German physician and anatomist. He was Professor of Anatomy at the Free University of Berlin from 1972 to 1998, and served as Dean of the Faculty of Medicine from 1980 to 1981. He was noted for his research on the fine structure of connective tissue, the morphology of hormone effects, and embryological and embryotoxic problems, and his research was central in the development of medical research utilising electron microscopy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merker#cite_note-3) Hans Georg Baumgarten noted on his death that he was "not only a chair-holder, but a philosopher, humanist, anthropologist, developmental biologist, transdisciplinary scholar and scientist".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merker#cite_note-BaumgartenHG-2)

## Background and education
[edit]
Merker was born in Merseburg, the son of a general practitioner. The Russian occupation saw his father thrown in jail by the communists, and as a son of an academic, he was banned from studying at universities in the Russian occupation zone. In December 1948, at 19, he enrolled as one of the first students at the newly established Free University of Berlin, which was founded in the same month with American support in West Berlin in response to the suppression of academic freedom by the communists at the Humboldt University. He initially studied art history and archeology, as the Free University did not yet have a preclinical medical programme. He started his studies of medicine in 1950 and settled permanently in West Berlin before the construction of the Berlin Wall, after which he did not see his parents for many years. He stayed for his entire career with the Free University, which he would later describe as "an island of freedom."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merker#cite_note-4)

## Background and education
Merker graduated as a physician at the Free University of Berlin in 1956. In 1957, he was employed at the Research Department of Electron Microscopy, which was headed by Willy Schwarz, at the Institute of Anatomy at the Free University of Berlin. He obtained his doctorate (Dr.med.) in 1958 and his Habilitation in 1964, and was appointed as Adjunct Professor (_außerplanmäßiger Professor_) at the Free University of Berlin in 1968. In 1969, he became director of the Research Department of Electron Microscopy. He held the first chair in anatomy from 1972 to 1998, in succession to Ernst von Herrath.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merker#cite_note-5) He also served as Dean of the Faculty of Medicine from 1980 to 1981, and was director of the Institute of Anatomy until 1998. He was a visiting scholar for one year at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel in 1965, and was subsequently a visiting scholar at universities in England and Sweden. He wrote more than 250 scientific papers. He became Professor Emeritus in 1998, and died in Berlin in 2014.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merker#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merker#cite_note-7)

## Selected publications
[edit]
*   _Risk assessment of prenatally – induced adverse health effects._ (with Neubert, Kavlock, and Klein, eds.), Springer – Verlag, Berlin et al., 1992.  
*   _Anatomie für Anästhesisten_, Blackwell – Wissenschaften, Berlin, 1990, ISBN978-3894121013  
*   _Elektronenmikroskopischer Atlas_, Blackwell – Wissenschaft, Berlin, 1989, ISBN978-3894120542  
*   _Anatomie für medizinische Hilfsberufe_, Walter de Gruyter, Berlin, 1989.  
*   _Teratology of the limbs_ (co-editor), Walter de Gruyter – Verlag, Berlin, 1981.  
*   _Culture techniques_ (with Neubert, eds.), Walter de Gruyter– Verlag, Berlin, 1981.  
*   _Methods in prenatal toxicology_ (with Neubert and Kwasigroch, eds.), G. Thieme, Stuttgart, 1977.

## Biography
Hans-Joachim Merks entered in 1937 in the II. Schiffsstammabteilung der Ostsee.
He was trained on board of the "Gorch Fock" and the "Schleswig-Holstein".
After different training courses he was transferred in 1941 to the minesweepers and was Kommandant of the "R 33" and the "R 34".
After beeing WIA in 1944 he was Kommandant of the "M 104" and after January 1945 he was promoted Flottillenchef der 2.Räumboots-Flottille.

21st September 1937 : Seekadett
1st May 1938 : Fähnrich zur See
1st July 1939 : Oberfähnrich zur See
1st August 1939 : Leutnant zur See
1st September 1941 : Oberleutnant zur See
1st April 1944 : Kapitänleutnant zur See

**Hans-Joachim Merks** (2 February 1917 – 21 February 1961) was a Kapitänleutnant with the Kriegsmarine during World War II and a recipient of the Knight's Cross of the Iron Cross (German language: [_Ritterkreuz des Eisernen Kreuzes_] Error: {{Lang}}: text has italic markup (help)). The Knight's Cross of the Iron Cross was awarded to recognise extreme battlefield bravery or successful military leadership.

## Awards[]
*   Iron Cross (1939)   
    *   2nd Class (20 November 1939)[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merks#cite_note-D%C3%B6rr_p57-1)  
    *   1st Class (22 May 1941)[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merks#cite_note-D%C3%B6rr_p57-1)

*   German Cross in Gold (21 November 1942)  
*   Minesweeper War Badge (12 November 1940)[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merks#cite_note-D%C3%B6rr_p57-1)  
*   Italian War Merit Cross with Swords (_Voce al valore militare_) (29 December 1942)[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merks#cite_note-D%C3%B6rr_p57-1)  
*   Cuff title "Afrika" (30 August 1943)[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merks#cite_note-D%C3%B6rr_p57-1)  
*   Wound Badge in Black (6 November 1944)[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merks#cite_note-D%C3%B6rr_p57-1)  
*   Knight's Cross of the Iron Cross (28 May 1945) [[a]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merks#endnote_Note1a)

## Footnotes[]
*   **a** There is no reference of the Knight's Cross awarded to Hans-Joachim Merks in the German National Archives. His personal file contains a letter from 1955 by the Deutsche Dienststelle (WASt), indicating that no proof of the award exists. The date was assigned by the Association of Knight's Cross Recipients (AKCR).[[2]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Hans-Joachim_Merks#cite_note-2)

## Biography
Hans-Joachim Merks entered in 1937 in the II. Schiffsstammabteilung der Ostsee.
He was trained on board of the "Gorch Fock" and the "Schleswig-Holstein".
After different training courses he was transferred in 1941 to the minesweepers and was Kommandant of the "R 33" and the "R 34".
After beeing WIA in 1944 he was Kommandant of the "M 104" and after January 1945 he was promoted Flottillenchef der 2.Räumboots-Flottille.
Promotions:
3rd April 1937 : Offiziersanwärter
21st September 1937 : Seekadett
1st May 1938 : Fähnrich zur See
1st July 1939 : Oberfähnrich zur See
1st August 1939 : Leutnant zur See
1st September 1941 : Oberleutnant zur See
1st April 1944 : Kapitänleutnant zur See
